chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Maliki narrated to us. He said: Mansur ibn al-Abbas narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever recites 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (Surah al-Ikhlas) sixty times in the first two units of the night prayer — thirty times in each unit — he will finish the prayer with no sin remaining between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.انفتل: To finish and turn away from prayer, indicating completion of the prayer
key_terms.صلاة الليل: Salat al-Layl — the voluntary night prayer, highly recommended in Shia practice
key_terms.قل هو الله أحد: Surah al-Ikhlas (Quran 112:1), the chapter of Divine Unity

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah al-Ikhlas in the night prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes the recitation of Surah al-Ikhlas (Quran 112) thirty times in each of the first two units of the night prayer (salat al-layl) as a means of total forgiveness. This teaching was delivered in the context of encouraging night worship, which holds special significance in Shia devotional practice as a voluntary prayer associated with spiritual purification.
word_analysis: he will finish (turn away from prayer)

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Ahmad al-Maliki narrated to us. He said: Mansur b. al-`Abbas narrated to us from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Hisham b. Salim from Zayd al-Shahham from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:
Whoever recites qul huwallahu ahad sixty times in the first two units of the night prayer (salat al-layl) – thirty times in each unit – he will be left with no sins between him and Allah.
